actions.text: DirMk("B:/Home"); CDC *SPCanvas=DCNew(32,32); DCFill(SPCanvas,TRANSPARENT); SPCanvas->color=BLACK; GrRect(SPCanvas,2,2,28,28); SPCanvas->color=YELLOW; GrRect(SPCanvas,4,4,24,24); SPCanvas->color=BLACK; GrRect(SPCanvas,8,9,5,5); GrRect(SPCanvas,19,9,5,5); GrRect(SPCanvas,9,21,14,4); U8 *SPRaw=DC2Sprite(SPCanvas); FileWrite("B:/Home/RobotSprite.SP",SPRaw,SpriteSize(SPRaw)); DCDel(SPCanvas); Free(SPRaw);

note: Create and save a native 32x32 transparent bitmap sprite with a yellow robot face.
Read the bundled game and replace only DrawX in a saved copy; load the native asset with FileRead and render it with Sprite3.
Inspect the saved native sprite asset in the shell.
Launch the saved game and inspect player1 robot preview in an empty upper-left square.
Move to the empty upper-right square and observe the same robot placement preview following the pointer.
Place player1 robot upper-left and move offboard to reveal the fixed mark and player2 O preview.
Click the occupied upper-left cell; reveal unchanged fixed robot and player2 preview after moving offboard.
Place player2 O in the center; rejection did not advance the turn.
Place a second robot upper-right and reveal two fixed robot marks plus center O.
Use the stock Ctrl-Alt-C exit and observe the shell.
Relaunch the saved source and persisted native sprite; observe a fresh empty board.
Repeat player1 upper-left robot placement after reload.
Repeat player2 center O placement after reload.
Repeat player1 upper-right robot placement; final live game retains two robots and center O.

actions.text: The saved game and native robot sprite reload correctly. Real clicks preserve turn order and reject an occupied square; the final board shows two robots and center O.

note: Finish with the saved modified game active. This reference is a scripted diagnostic, not a model trial.
